t.ETHYLHEXYL_METHOXYCINNAMATE.agn: In the EU it may be used as a UV filter at up to 10% (Annex VI, entry 12). It is on the EU priority list of potential endocrine disruptors (group B).
t.ETHYLHEXYL_METHOXYCINNAMATE.eff.0: Listed among substances to be assessed by the EU for possible effects on the hormone system; this entry holds no substance-specific conclusion from an agency.
t.ETHYLHEXYL_METHOXYCINNAMATE.k3.0: EU priority list of potential endocrine disruptors (group B). On the 28-substance priority list that the European Commission drew up in 2019 for potential endocrine disruptors in cosmetics (substances suspected of possibly affecting the hormone system), in Group B. The assessment of part of this group is ongoing; the status of substances that have been concluded is stated separately. The list is not a ruling; it shows the order of assessment.
t.ETHYLHEXYL_METHOXYCINNAMATE.reg.0: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex VI, entry 12: Permitted UV filter, with an upper limit.
t.ETHYLHEXYL_METHOXYCINNAMATE.summary: A common UVB filter in sunscreens.
